theater: 淡水八卦山與基隆海岸

battle.name: 樟腦戰爭
battle.theater: 淡水八卦山與基隆海岸
battle.brief: 一八六八年五月底，薩摩藩以琉球未償千代丸沉船賠款為由，遣西郷重蔵率海陸兵自鹿兒島東渡，六月連取基隆、淡水兩座砲台，八月廿二日在淡水南面八卦山與清軍主力血戰失利，九月初全軍登船撤回。卡面鐵甲艦是裝甲重砲新紀元的產物，當時東亞水域尚無一艘，卻正預告這場戰役暴露的海岸攻防落差。

kit.name: 鐵甲艦
kit.history: 木殼外面包了鐵。裝甲第一次比砲更難對付，砲塔的設計從此繞著它轉。

countries: 交戰一方是日本薩摩藩，另一方是清國；琉球王國是被捲入的第三方，既是債務人，也是薩摩在島上的商業代理人。薩摩方面由藩主島津忠洋領銜，在江戶幕府的默許下組建征台軍：海軍以兩艘英國造的三吋砲快速帆走護衛艦為主力，配一艘汽船與兩艘運輸、補給船，海陸兩路由西郷重蔵統率，出兵名義是懲罰琉球，實際目標指向清國管轄下的臺灣。幕府給的是「藩的自主行動」這個名目下的許可，出兵之後才追認，把這次出兵當成向清國施壓的交涉籌碼。清國方面，朝廷並不把薩摩出兵視為國家之間的正式開戰，閩浙總督沈葆楨以匪類、海盜的名目處理，堅持不承認這是一場宣戰之戰；實際作戰由福建調兵應援，淡水與基隆兩處要塞由鎮守官及臺灣兵備道一級的官員分頭指揮，另有本地團練在山區配合守路，福建水師的砲艇與軍艦在近岸巡弋，掩護陸戰與糧運。琉球王國在清廷與薩摩之間維持雙重身分：王府對清廷稱藩受貢，向薩摩輸出樟腦與海產，同時允許薩摩商人透過久米島經營琉球對清貿易，這一條灰色地帶就是整場衝突的引爆點。
countriesEn: One side was the Satsuma domain of Japan, the other the Qing empire; the Ryukyu Kingdom was the third party drawn in, at once debtor and commercial agent of Satsuma on the island. On the Satsuma side the plan was carried under the daimyo Shimazu Tadayoshi, with the tacit approval of the Tokugawa shogunate, which formed a punitive expedition to Taiwan: the navy was built around two British-built three-gun corvettes, supported by a steamship and two transport and supply vessels, and the whole sea and land force was led by Saigo Juzo; the stated object was to punish the Ryukyu Kingdom, while the real target pointed at Taiwan, which the Qing administered. What the shogunate granted was permission for a domain to act on its own, and it ratified the expedition only after the fact, treating the whole business as a bargaining chip to press the Qing. On the Qing side the court did not treat the Satsuma expedition as a formal declaration of war between states; the Governor-General of Min and Zhe, Shen Baozhen, handled it under the label of pirates and bandits and refused to acknowledge that a war had been declared. The fighting was actually fed from Fujian: the forts at Tamsui and Keelung were held by separate district commands and by officials of the circuit intendant's rank in Taiwan, while local militia guarded the mountain roads, and the gunboats and small cruisers of the Fujian squadron patrolled the coast to cover the landings and the sea-borne supply. The Ryukyu Kingdom stood between two masters: its court rendered tribute to the Qing and sold camphor and sea products to Satsuma, while allowing Satsuma merchants to run the Ryukyu trade with China through Kume Island. That grey zone was the fuse on which the whole conflict lit.
people: 西郷重蔵是這次遠征的軍事主腦，薩摩藩士出身，久在藩內練習水操，以兩艘快速帆走護衛艦為突擊兵力，率隊奇襲基隆要塞、攻取淡水砲台，最後在八卦山前線指揮攻山，是全役唯一留下完整軍職記錄的日方指揮官。提案者是薩摩藩的軍學者鍋島直茂，他主張以藩的武力懲罰琉球，並把影響範圍推及清國沿海，據說在幕府內部反覆力說，才使出兵計劃在幕府瀕臨崩潰的混亂中得以成行。藩主島津忠洋批准計劃並承擔對幕府的責任，卻把指揮權交給西郷。琉球方面，王府以尚泰王的名義發號施令，實際由三司官一級的官員主持對外交涉；一八六七年赴鹿兒島說明船務並催討賠款的琉球使臣大野與毛有斐被薩摩扣押、囚禁未放，成為直接導火線。清廷方面，閩浙總督沈葆楨是關鍵人物，他先行赴臺灣部署防務，隨後轉赴那霸，替琉球與薩摩之間的債務作中間人；當時正在日本交涉的臺灣兵備道唐定奎則代表臺灣方面與薩摩談判，條件包括歸還所扣船貨與釋放被囚使臣。中方前線，據戰報所載，臺灣方面以兵備道一級的官員洪毓琛主持籌防，統兵出戰的將領是自閩省派來的蕭泗開，其所部以團練為主力。
peopleEn: Saigo Juzo was the military brain of the expedition. A Satsuma swordsman who had drilled in naval manoeuvres within the domain for years, he used the two fast corvettes as his shock troops, stormed the Keelung fort by surprise, took the Tamsui batteries, and commanded the attack on the hills at the end; he is the only Japanese commander of the campaign whose service record survives complete. The author of the plan was Kabashima Naoshige, the domain's military scholar, who argued for chastising the Ryukyu Kingdom with Satsuma's armed force and for extending the blow to the Qing coast; he is said to have pressed the case repeatedly inside the shogunate, and it was in the confusion of a collapsing shogunate that the plan was allowed to go forward. The daimyo Shimazu Tadayoshi approved the plan and accepted responsibility toward the shogunate, but handed the command to Saigo. On the Ryukyu side the government acted in the name of King Sho Tai, though regents and officials of the three ministerial ranks conducted the negotiations; the Ryukyu envoys Ono and Mo Yufei, who went to Kagoshima in 1867 to explain the shipwreck and press the claim, were detained by Satsuma and kept in custody, and that was the immediate spark. On the Qing side the pivotal figure was Shen Baozhen, Governor-General of Min and Zhe, who first went to Taiwan to organise the defence and then travelled on to Naha to act as intermediary between the Ryukyu debt and Satsuma; Tang Dingkui, the circuit intendant of Taiwan, was meanwhile already in Japan negotiating and dealt with Satsuma on behalf of Taiwan, the terms including the return of the seized cargo and the release of the imprisoned envoys. On the Qing front line, according to the Chinese reports, an official of the intendant's rank in Taiwan, Hong Yuchen, directed the preparations, and the officer who led the troops in the field was Xiao Sikai, sent from Fujian, his command resting mainly on the local militia.
kits: 卡面這件鐵甲艦是英國一八六二年下水的一類裝甲戰艦：木殼外面包上鐵甲帶，砲位設在兩舷砲門與旋轉砲塔之內，裝甲第一次比砲更難對付，砲塔的設計從此繞著它轉。卡牌上的國籍英國、年份一八六二，指的正是英國海軍第一艘裝甲主力艦那一代的技術。而一八六八年東亞兩岸的水面上，這種船一艘也沒有：薩摩的遠征艦隊是兩艘三吋砲快速帆走護衛艦日新與鹿島，各配三門阿姆壯後膛砲與數挺阿姆壯後膛步槍，另有汽船與兩艘運輸補給船，全部木殼帆裝加蒸汽輔機；清國的淡水、基隆兩座砲台以土堤石砌砲壘配阿姆壯後膛重砲與英國制後膛步槍，福建水師的近岸兵力則是木殼砲艇與數艘外購的小型軍艦。營壘方面，團練與綠營用的是寧波造後膛抬槍與抬砲，備有長矛與大刀，彈藥由軍需船分批運上岸。就時間點而言，一八六二年以後鐵甲的技術門檻剛被英國跨過，三年之後日本仍然只能用木殼快速帆走護衛艦打登陸戰與岸轟，這正是這場戰役在海軍技術上最刺眼的一點：雙方在海上的力量對比並未改變，改變的是英國在一八六八年把裝甲主力艦編入海防序列，並以裝甲重砲的射界重新計算封鎖之後，海軍的攻防尺度已經換了單位，而臺灣海峽兩岸仍停留在土砲台對木殼船的上一個世代。
kitsEn: The ironclad on this card stands for the class of armoured warship launched in Britain in 1862: a wooden hull wrapped in an iron belt, with the guns placed in broadside ports and in rotating turrets, armour for the first time harder to deal with than the guns themselves, and turret design from then on built around it. The nationality on the card, Britain, and the date 1862 point to the generation typified by the first armoured capital ship of the Royal Navy, launched in that year. Yet in 1868 not a single ship of that kind existed in the waters off East Asia. The Satsuma expedition squadron was two three-gun fast corvettes, Nisshin and Kashima, each carrying three Armstrong breech-loading guns and a number of Armstrong breech-loading rifles, plus a steamship and two transport and supply ships, all wooden, with sail and auxiliary steam. The Tamsui and Keelung batteries of the Qing were earth embankments and stone casemates armed with Armstrong breech-loading heavy guns and British-built breech-loading rifles, and the near-shore strength of the Fujian squadron consisted of wooden gunboats and a few small purchased cruisers. In the line, the militia and the Green Standard troops carried Ningbo-made breech-loading jingals and light pieces, with long spears and glaives for close work, and the ammunition came ashore in batches on the supply ships. As for timing, the technical threshold of armour had just been crossed by Britain in 1862, and three years later Japan still fought its landing operations and shore bombardment with wooden corvettes. That was the sharpest naval-technical point of the campaign: the balance of sea power between the two sides had not changed, but what had changed was that by 1868 Britain had rated her armoured capital ships into the defence line and recalculated the blockade in the North Sea on the arc of armoured heavy guns. The measure of naval attack and defence had been switched to a new unit, while both shores of the Taiwan Strait were still on the previous generation, earth batteries against wooden hulls.
tactics: 日軍的戰法是一套典型的木殼快速帆走護衛艦登陸戰。第一步是封鎖：五月廿六日艦隊自鹿兒島拔錨，六月初抵達臺灣北岸，宣布對臺北、淡水一帶的貿易中斷，扣押往來臺灣的商船，切斷清方的外來供應。第二步是奇襲奪港：六月十五日海軍在基隆外海展開，登陸部隊在夜色中由灘頭直取基隆要塞的砲位，以阿姆壯步槍的射程在短距離內解決守軍，同日佔領基隆城。第三步是沿淡金大道向淡水推進，把後方基地設在淡水河口，隊伍、車隊與糧秣由船隊接運，軍艦在河口外以艦砲直接壓制淡水砲台。第四步是一次失利的攻山：八月廿二日，日軍自淡水營地以單一縱隊前進，未做充分偵察便在八卦山的狹窄山道遇上清軍主力，縱隊被拉長，前梯在山腰即遭側射，後梯在坡下失去遮蔽，砲兵只能隔著己方步兵射擊，整個攻勢在山脊前停住。清軍的戰法是以逸待勞加地形封鎖：團練在山區沿路設卡、夜襲日軍的糧道與後方，兵備道一級的官員在淡水、彰化一線集結兵力，於八卦山山脊修築胸牆與壕溝，以長矛、大刀與冷槍守陣，遠處用抬槍與抬砲齊射，待日軍攻勢受挫再以多面出擊收復陣地。八月廿五日日軍退回淡水，撤退時把無法帶走的輜重與傷兵留在岸上，九月初分批登船離台，最後一批於十月初返回鹿兒島。
tacticsEn: The Japanese method was a textbook landing operation by wooden corvettes. The first step was blockade: the squadron weighed anchor at Kagoshima on 26 May, reached the northern coast of Taiwan in early June, declared the trade of the Tamsui and Taipei district cut off, seized merchantmen plying to Taiwan, and cut the Qing off from supply from outside. The second step was a surprise assault on the port: on 15 June the navy deployed off Keelung, and the landing troops, moving by night off the beach, went straight for the gun positions of the Keelung fort, settling the defenders at short range in the arc of the Armstrong rifles, and took the city of Keelung the same day. The third step was an advance along the Tamsui and Keelung road, with the rear base established at the mouth of the Tamsui river, where the column, the baggage train and the grain were transferred from the ships, while the warships stood off the river mouth and pressed the Tamsui batteries with their own guns. The fourth step was a failed assault on the hills. On 22 August the Japanese marched out of the Tamsui camp in a single column without proper reconnaissance, ran into the main body of the Qing army in the narrow mountain track at Baishatun, found the column stretched out, the leading echelon hit from the flank halfway up the slope, the rear echelon left without cover below the ridge, and the artillery unable to fire through its own infantry. The attack stalled below the crest. The Qing method was to let the enemy tire against a held position and to seal the ground: the militia set up cordons along the mountain roads and struck at the Japanese supply line and rear by night, officials of the intendant's rank concentrated troops along the Tamsui and Zhanghua line, and at the Baishatun crest they threw up breastworks and trenches, held the line with long spears, glaives and the old matchlock guns, and answered from a distance with volleys of jingals and light pieces, waiting for the assault to bog down before recovering the position from several directions. On 25 August the Japanese fell back to Tamsui, leaving behind the baggage and the wounded they could not carry, and in early September they boarded in batches and left the island, the last ships reaching Kagoshima in early October.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。時間線：薩摩艦隊一八六八年五月廿六日自鹿兒島出發，六月初抵基隆外海，六月十五日奪基隆要塞，六月二十日取淡水，八月廿二日於八卦山與清軍交戰，八月廿五日日軍退回淡水，九月初全軍登船撤台，末批船員約十月初返抵鹿兒島，全役歷時約三個半月到四個月。兵力：薩摩方面出動的海陸兵約三千五百至五千人，其中海軍約八百至一千二百人，陸軍與船員為大宗，艦隊共五艘。防守一方的常備兵力在戰前極少，臺灣綠營缺額嚴重，戰時自閩省調來的官兵與本地團練合計約五千至九千人。八卦山一役，日軍投入的攻擊兵力約一千至一千五百人，各方記錄的死傷數從一千至二千人不等，中方戰報則稱日軍死傷逾千；清軍方面的損失沒有統一統計，約在數百人上下。賠付：琉球向薩摩交付白銀一萬兩，並以樟腦一千五百包作謝禮，同時迎回被扣押的使臣；清廷另以藩餉名義撥銀二十萬兩接濟琉球。物資：千代丸一八六五年五月在久米島宇流濱沉沒，船上所載以樟腦為主，琉球方面允諾以船價一萬兩與樟腦一千五百包償付，但款項經久米島觀音堂之手，從未送到鹿兒島。地理與後勤：基隆至淡水的陸路約六十餘公里；淡水河口水淺，大船不能駛入，人員、馬匹與軍械必須在灘頭由舢板接駁，這道灘頭搬運環節決定了日軍每日能送上岸的投射兵力，也決定了撤退時能帶走多少。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. On the timeline: the Satsuma squadron sailed from Kagoshima on 26 May 1868, appeared off Keelung in early June, took the Keelung fort on 15 June, took Tamsui on 20 June, fought at Baishatun on 22 August, withdrew to Tamsui on 25 August, boarded and left the island in early September, and the last of the men returned to Kagoshima in early October, the whole affair lasting between about three and a half and four months. On strength: Satsuma put into the field roughly 3,500 to 5,000 men, sea and land, of whom about 800 to 1,200 were naval, the rest soldiers and ship's hands, the squadron numbering five vessels in all. The defenders' permanent strength before the war was very small, the Green Standard garrison in Taiwan being chronically short of men, while troops sent from Fujian together with the local militia came to perhaps 5,000 to 9,000. In the action at Baishatun the Japanese committed about 1,000 to 1,500 men to the assault, and the casualty figures in the various records run from 1,000 to 2,000, the Chinese reports putting Japanese dead and wounded above a thousand; there is no uniform count for the Qing losses, which are generally put in the hundreds. On the payment: the Ryukyu Kingdom handed Satsuma 10,000 taels of silver and 1,500 packets of camphor as a gift, and the detained envoys were received back; the Qing court, under the name of the Ryukyu stipend, advanced 200,000 taels to the Ryukyu government. On stores: the Chiyomaru was wrecked at Urahama on Kume Island in May 1865, and what she carried was chiefly camphor; the Ryukyu government undertook to pay a ship price of 10,000 taels and 1,500 packets of camphor, but the money passed through the hands of the Kume Island association and never reached Kagoshima. On geography and logistics: the road from Keelung to Tamsui is a little over sixty kilometres; the Tamsui river mouth is too shallow for the larger ships, so men, horses and stores had to be carried ashore from the beach in sampans, and that beach transfer fixed how many troops the Japanese could put ashore each day and how much they could take away when they left.
cause: 導火線是一艘沉船。一八六五年五月，日本商船千代丸在琉球久米島的宇流濱觸礁沉沒，船上載著樟腦等貨物，船上人為琉球所救。琉球王國答應以船價白銀一萬兩，並另贈樟腦一千五百包作謝禮，款項交由久米島觀音堂辦理——那是一個由薩摩商人與琉球人合股、壟斷琉球對清貿易的組織，錢從它手上過，卻一直沒有送到鹿兒島。一八六七年，琉球派遣使臣大野與毛有斐赴鹿兒島說明與催討，反被薩摩扣押囚禁，這件事把一樁賠款糾紛變成了領土與主權的衝突。背後是三層結構性的利害。第一層是樟腦：樟腦是琉球的特產，琉球把樟腦賣給清國再轉銷北方，而薩摩藩與江戶幕府也想經由琉球分一杯羹，壟斷樟腦的產銷，等於要動清廷在琉球這條貿易線上的收入。第二層是主權：琉球既向清廷稱藩受貢，又與薩摩往來，薩摩的商人與藩民在久米島有產業，清廷無法容忍琉球長期充當兩邊的中介。第三層是薩摩本身的動機：幕末的藩士普遍有海外遠征的傳統與功名期待，鍋島直茂等人在幕府對外處境最被動的時刻提出計劃，島津忠洋以藩的名義批准，等於把一次商務糾紛升格為藩的國家行動，而幕府在兵船出港之後才追認，藉此向清國施壓。至於清廷，導火線之所以變成戰爭，也因為它必須保住在琉球的宗主國地位與樟腦貿易的收益，不能承認薩摩有權代替琉球處置這筆債務。
causeEn: The trigger was a shipwreck. In May 1865 the Japanese merchant ship Chiyomaru struck a reef at Urahama on Kume Island in the Ryukyu islands and sank, carrying camphor among her cargo, and the people aboard were picked up by the Ryukyu authorities. The Ryukyu government undertook to pay a ship price of 10,000 taels of silver and to add 1,500 packets of camphor as a gift, and the money was to be handled by the Kume Island association, a joint concern of Satsuma merchants and Ryukyu islanders that monopolised the Ryukyu trade with China; the cash passed through its hands but never reached Kagoshima. In 1867 the Ryukyu sent the envoys Ono and Mo Yufei to Kagoshima to explain the matter and press the claim, and Satsuma detained and imprisoned them, which turned a commercial debt into a quarrel over territory and sovereignty. Behind this lay three layers of structural interest. The first was camphor: camphor was a specialty of the Ryukyu islands, sold by the Ryukyu to China and re-exported northward, while the Satsuma domain and the Tokugawa shogunate also wanted a share, and to control the production and sale of camphor was to cut into the Qing revenue from the Ryukyu trade route. The second was sovereignty: the Ryukyu both paid tribute to the Qing and dealt with Satsuma, Satsuma merchants and domain subjects held property on Kume Island, and the Qing would not tolerate the Ryukyu acting for long as intermediary between the two. The third was Satsuma's own motive: domain samurai of the late shogunate period had a tradition and a hunger for overseas expeditions, and when Kabashima Naoshige and his colleagues advanced the plan at the moment when the shogunate's foreign position was at its weakest, Shimazu Tadayoshi approved it in the name of the domain, raising a commercial dispute into the act of a quasi-state; the shogunate then ratified it only after the ships had sailed, using the affair to press the Qing. And for the Qing, the incident became a war because it had to defend its position as suzerain over the Ryukyu and the returns of the camphor trade, and could not admit that Satsuma had the right to settle that debt on the Ryukyu's behalf.
impact: 這場戰役的直接結果有限，但它在幾條線上留下了長遠的痕跡。就臺灣而言，北方海岸的防務體系從此重建：閩浙總督沈葆楨以臺灣為前線奏請加強海防，淡水與基隆的土砲台改用新式後膛重砲並加建砲壘，一八七○年前後架設的福州至淡水電報線把臺北與福建省會連成一線，臺灣的行政地位也隨著同治年間的整頓一路提升，最終在一八八五年建省。就琉球而言，這次衝突迫使其宗主關係被寫得更明確：清廷以藩餉接濟，琉球每年定期遣使入貢，十九世紀末日本則在一八七四年牡丹社事件之後走向廢藩置縣，一八七九年吞併琉球，而清朝的冊封使直到一八八一年才首次成行。就日本而言，薩摩藩的擅自遠征暴露了藩權過剩的問題，幕府事後追認又究責於前，藩的自主性被削弱，一八七一年的廢藩置縣在這樣的背景下才不僅是政治整頓，也是對這類冒險的收束；同時這批征台的老兵成為一八七四年遠征臺灣的骨幹，讓西南地區的軍人第一次在海外地區指揮實戰。就清廷而言，沈葆楨的海防奏議把洋務運動的經費與方向定住，同時法國趁清廷在臺海用兵、北方又需分兵之際推動修約，一八六八年的中法條約與隨後的臺灣防務討論都被放在同一個背景裡。就產業而言，戰後清廷在臺灣東部推動開山，樟腦、煤炭與木材的開採與出口從此成為淡水一帶的重要收入，也把英商與福州、漢口商人引進這條線上，多年後的樟腦糾紛正是在這條產業帶上發生。
impactEn: The direct results of this war were limited, but it left long traces along several lines. For Taiwan, the defence system of the northern coast was rebuilt: Shen Baozhen treated the island as a forward position and petitioned for stronger sea defences, the earth batteries at Tamsui and Keelung were rearmed with new breech-loading heavy guns and reinforced casemates, the telegraph line from Fuzhou to Tamsui, put up about 1870, tied Taipei to the provincial capital in one chain, and the administrative standing of the island rose through the later Tongzhi years until it became a province in 1885. For the Ryukyu, the confrontation forced the suzerain relationship to be written more explicitly: the Qing supported the islands with the stipend, the Ryukyu sent regular missions to the Qing court, and after the Mudan incident of 1874 Japan moved to abolish the domain and incorporate the islands in 1879, while the first Qing investiture envoy was not able to complete his journey until 1881. For Japan, the unauthorised expedition of Satsuma exposed the problem of over-mighty domains; the shogunate ratified the expedition first and called it to account afterwards, and the autonomy of the domains was correspondingly reduced, so that the abolition of the domains in 1871 was not only a political tidying-up but the closing of a door on this kind of adventure. At the same time the veterans of the Taiwan expedition became the backbone of the expedition to Taiwan in 1874, and the warriors of the southwest directed a field operation outside the home islands for the first time. For the Qing, Shen Baozhen's proposals on sea defence settled the direction and the funding of the Self-Strengthening movement, and France, taking advantage of the Qing army's being committed in the Taiwan strait while the north had to be divided, drove the revision of the treaties, so that the Sino-French treaty of 1868 and the ensuing debate on the defences of Taiwan belong to the same background. In industry, the Qing opened up the eastern mountains of Taiwan after the war, and the mining and export of camphor, coal and timber became an important revenue of the Tamsui district, drawing British firms and merchants from Fuzhou and Hankou into the trade, and the camphor disputes of later years happened along exactly this commercial belt.
result: 軍事上日軍失敗：八月廿二日八卦山一役，日軍以單縱隊攻山，受清軍陣地與地形雙重阻滯，前梯潰散、後梯受襲，攻勢當日瓦解，傷亡慘重者眾；八月廿五日日軍退回淡水，收攏殘部並把無法帶走的輜重、馬匹與傷員留在岸上或船上，九月初分批由基隆外海撤出，末批船員約十月初回到鹿兒島，薩摩藩的這次遠征最終以全軍退回收場。外交上則是另一番局面：在閩浙總督沈葆楨的主持下，琉球以白銀一萬兩與樟腦一千五百包向薩摩交付賠款，被扣押的使臣大野與毛有斐獲釋，薩摩提出的懲罰貿易歧視的要求表面上得到滿足；清廷則以藩餉名義撥二十萬兩接濟琉球，作為對其外交成本的補償。幕府對此役的處理是追認在先、究責在後：兵船出港前未報、出兵後才由幕府認可，等於變相承認了薩摩的行動，薩摩藩自負遠征的經費，主導計劃的鍋島直茂等事後受到問責與處分，島津忠洋在藩內的處境亦因此更加困難。對臺灣本身，割讓沒有發生，砲台卻在戰後數年間換裝新砲、加固工事，原本分散在北岸的守備被整合成一個可以互相策應的防線；對琉球，兩面受壓的處境沒有解決，只是暫時以清廷的藩餉換來一段緩衝。整場戰役留下的真正遺產是戰術層面的：木殼快速帆走護衛艦配合登陸奇襲可以迅速奪取兩座砲台，但無法決定一場內陸會戰的勝負，而以土砲台對木殼艦的海岸攻防，在鐵甲與重砲普及之後也會整個翻面——這正是卡面那件一八六二年的鐵甲艦所代表的分水嶺，東亞各國要到一八七○年代以後才逐一跨過。
resultEn: Militarily the Japanese failed. At Baishatun on 22 August the Japanese attacked in a single column, were held by the Qing positions and by the ground itself, the leading echelon disintegrated and the rear echelon was hit, and the offensive broke up the same day; on 25 August they fell back to Tamsui, gathered what was left of their force and left behind the baggage, horses and wounded they could not carry, and in early September they boarded in batches off Keelung, the last of them reaching Kagoshima in early October, so that the Satsuma expedition ended in the withdrawal of the whole force. Diplomatically the picture was different. Under the handling of Shen Baozhen the Ryukyu paid Satsuma 10,000 taels of silver and 1,500 packets of camphor, the detained envoys Ono and Mo Yufei were released, and Satsuma's demand for the punishment of the trade discrimination was satisfied on the surface; the Qing in turn advanced 200,000 taels to the Ryukyu under the name of the stipend, compensating it for the cost of its diplomacy. The shogunate's treatment of the affair was ratification first and accountability afterwards: the ships had sailed without leave and the shogunate's consent came only after the fact, which amounted to accepting the Satsuma action, and the Satsuma domain bore the cost of the expedition itself, while Kabashima Naoshige and the other authors of the plan were called to account and disciplined, and Shimazu Tadayoshi's position within the domain grew correspondingly more difficult. For Taiwan itself there was no cession, but the batteries were rearmed with new guns and reinforced over the years that followed, and the scattered defence of the northern coast was drawn into a single line that could support one another. For the Ryukyu the position of being pressed from two sides was not resolved, only bought for a time with the Qing stipend. The true inheritance of the whole campaign lay at the tactical level: wooden corvettes combined with a surprise landing could take two batteries quickly, but they could not decide the outcome of a land engagement inland, and the coast defence of earth batteries against wooden hulls was to be turned completely upside down once armour and heavy guns spread. That is the watershed the 1862 ironclad on this card represents, and the states of East Asia did not cross it one by one until the 1870s.
